title: Departments
markdown:
**What it is:** The org units the Executive works through. Each department has goals, an authority level, a head, and a specialist agent behind it.

**What it does:**

- View every department with its goal count and health (on-track / at-risk / off-track).
- Create departments and give them a mission, goals, budget, and headcount.
- Set the **authority level** — act automatically, propose for approval, or always escalate.
- Wire up a head person and team channels (Slack, Discord, Telegram).

**How to use:**

1. Open **Departments** and click **+ Add department**. Enter a **Name** (and, optionally, a mission) and click **Create**. New departments start at *Proposes, you approve*.
2. Open the department and click **Edit settings**:
   - **Department head** — the person who owns it.
   - **Authority level** — **Acts on its own**, **Proposes, you approve**, or **Escalates to a human**.
   - **Recurring check-in** — when the department checks in. New departments check in `daily@09:00`; change it to e.g. `daily@14:00` or `weekly@mon@09:00` (times are UTC).
   - **Headcount** and **Budget (USD)**.
   - **Team channels** — a Slack channel ID, Discord channel ID or Telegram chat ID. Leave them blank and messages go to the department head by DM.
   - **Watched entities** — one per line.

   Then click **Save settings**.
3. Click **+ Add Goal**: pick a timeframe (week, month, quarter, year, or ongoing), enter the **Key result** and **Target** (and current progress if you know it), set a status, and click **Add Goal**. Each goal has **Edit** and **Delete**.
4. Keep goals current by just telling the Executive what happened — it updates the matching goal and records why.
5. Set a new goal the same way: tell the Executive the target, and it adds the goal under the right department (or area), creating that department if you don't have one yet. Only the owner can do this, from the web app or their own Slack or Discord — a teammate, or an email, can't. It adds one goal for each target you actually give it (at most 8 per department this way) — ask it to "set up some goals" and it asks you which ones.

**Examples from chat:** *"We closed 40% of the Q3 ARR target."* · *"We lost the Acme deal."* · *"New Sales goal: 20 paying customers by December 31."* · *"Make Sarah the head of Marketing."*

**Goals page:** **Goals** in the sidebar (under **You** when you use Open Executive just for yourself) lists every goal in one place, grouped by **area** — an area is what a department is called there. Each goal shows its status, timeframe, target and where it stands now, with **Edit** and **Delete**. Click **+ Add goal**, pick the **Area** it belongs to, and fill it in as above; areas with no goals yet are listed under **Other areas** so you can start one there. The page works the same when you use it with your team — it's just not in the team sidebar.

**Just for yourself?** In that mode department check-ins are paused and the sidebar shows **Goals** instead of **Departments**. The departments are still there — open `/departments` to rename an area or change its settings.

*Note: the authority level is what decides whether the Executive acts on its own or asks first within that department's scope.*
